title: Executor ON/OFF Dashboard — durable operator intent for supported executors (PAIR_NATIVE/CODEX/DEVIN/DSH) surfaced under Mission Control Settings; OFF blocks every new dispatch path without cancelling running work
description: Executor ON/OFF for the Mission Control dashboard. Canonical state: executor.status (ENABLED/DISABLED) — the field CapabilityRouter already rejects at route time (EXECUTOR_DISABLED, gate 1). New seams: (a) ExecutorRegistry.setExecutorEnabled flips status inside one immediate txn with OCC retry + audited EXECUTOR_ENABLED/EXECUTOR_DISABLED journal events (idempotent repeat writes no event); (b) GovernedTaskGate.dispatch_governed_task re-proves status before adapter.dispatch — covers the adoption path that bypasses the router for a VALIDATED/authorized governed task whose dispatch never ran; proven EXECUTION_PERSISTED history still returns early so OFF never cancels running work; (c) registerGovernedExecutors + the PAIR_NATIVE register now treat a persisted status as operator intent that survives every restart, with options.default_disabled supplying product defaults (production seeds DEVIN+DSH OFF, CODEX+PAIR_NATIVE ON); (d) GET /api/executors projects the supported set with enabled/availability/qualification/auth/bound/requires_restart/missing_prerequisites (volatile fields come from the normalized descriptor, never the raw row), and POST /api/executors/:id/state mutates under the existing MC-token + x-operator-id operator authority; (e) Settings page gains a compact Executor Management section (live-refreshed, confirmation on disable, honest missing-prereq/restart hints). No second routing system; no planner/CEO coupling; Hermes intentionally absent.
